question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{{x}^{5}},\, & x\ge 1 \\ 0,\, & x<1\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<1 \\ h(x),\, & x\ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $x\ge 1,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ {\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{x}\frac{4}{{t}^{5}}\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={-\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}|}_{1}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}+1 \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1, \\ 1-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$
